# 1 Enoch Chapter 91 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all verses in 1 Enoch Chapter 91 where the three translators (EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA) significantly diverged in their renderings, along with SOPHIA's resolution and reasoning.

---

## 91:3 — 'hearken aright' vs. 'listen rightly' vs. 'hear' — register of exhortation

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "hearken aright to-the-voice of-my-mouth" | Archaic English preserves the solemn register of Ge'ez wisdom instruction |
| LOGOS | "listen rightly to the voice of my mouth" | Modern equivalent; preserves the dual command (hear + listen correctly) |
| PNEUMA | "hear every word your father speaks" | Compressed; functionally equivalent in modern English |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted 'listen rightly to the voice of my mouth' (LOGOS). The Ge'ez has two distinct imperatives — 'hear' and 'attend correctly.' EMET's 'hearken' is unnecessarily archaic. PNEUMA's compression loses the second command. The testamentary genre (father's final words) warrants formal language.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Genre-significant — testamentary literature register.

---

## 91:4 — 'double heart' vs. 'divided heart' vs. 'divided loyalties'

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a-double heart" | Literal Ge'ez: kilé lebb — 'two hearts' |
| LOGOS | "a divided heart" | English idiom for duplicity; cf. James 1:8 dipsuchos |
| PNEUMA | "divided loyalties" | Modern paraphrase; 'loyalties' makes the ethical implication explicit |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted 'a divided heart' (LOGOS). The Ge'ez 'two hearts' is a Semitic idiom for duplicity (cf. Psalm 12:2 be-lev va-lev). 'Divided heart' preserves the body metaphor while being naturally English. PNEUMA's 'divided loyalties' loses the heart imagery.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Idiomatic — Semitic body metaphor preserved.

---
